questions.q: What will be the effect on the root mean square velocity of oxygen molecules if the temperature is doubled and oxygen molecule dissociates into atomic oxygen?
options: The velocity of atomic oxygen remains same
The velocity of atomic oxygen doubles
The velocity of atomic oxygen becomes half
The velocity of atomic oxygen becomes four times
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The RMS velocity of a gas is given by, ${v}_{RMS} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

When ${O}_{2}$~dissociates into $O$~its~molecular mass becomes $\dfrac{M}{2}$. Therefore,

Ratio of RMS~speed,~$\dfrac{v1}{v2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{T1}{T2} \times \dfrac{M2}{M1}}⇒ \dfrac{v1}{v2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{2T} \times \dfrac{M / 2}{M}}⇒ \dfrac{v2}{v1} = 2$

questions.q: A polyatomic ideal gas has $24$ vibrational modes. What is the value of $\gamma ?$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since each vibrational mode has $2$ degrees of freedom hence total vibrational degrees of freedom $= 48$

$f = 3 + 3 + 48 = 54$

$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f} = \dfrac{28}{27} = 1 . 03$

questions.q: An ideal gas occupies a volume of $2m^{3}$ at a pressure of $3 \times {10}^{6}Pa .$ The energy of the gas is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$V = 2m^{3}$

$P = 3 \times {10}^{6}Pa$

$PV = nRT$

$E = \dfrac{f}{2}nRT = \dfrac{f}{2}PV = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 3 \times {10}^{6} \times 2$

$= 9 \times {10}^{6}J$

questions.q: To raise the temperature of a certain mass of gas by $50 ° C$ at a constant pressure,$160$~calories of heat is required. When the same mass of gas is cooled by $100 ° C$ at constant volume,$240$ calories of heat is released. How many degrees of freedom does each molecule of this gas have (assume gas to be ideal)?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At constant pressure :

$∆ Q = {nC}_{P} ∆ T$~$⇒ 160 = {nC}_{P} . 50$~ .....(1)

At constant volume

$∆ Q = {nC}_{v} ∆ T$~$⇒ 240 = {nC}_{v} . 100$......(2)

Equation (1) divided by (2)

$\dfrac{160}{240} = \dfrac{CP}{CV} \cdot \dfrac{50}{100}$

$\dfrac{CP}{CV} = \dfrac{4}{3} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f}$

$f = 6$

questions.q: Two vessels $A$ and $B$ are of the same size and are at same temperature. $A$ contains $1g$ of hydrogen and $B$ contains $1g$ of oxygen. ${P}_{A}$ and ${P}_{B}$ are the pressures of the gases in $A$ and $B$ respectively, then $\dfrac{PA}{PB}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For both the gases, it follows that

$\dfrac{{P}_{A}{V}_{A}}{{P}_{B}{V}_{B}} = \dfrac{{n}_{A}R{T}_{A}}{{n}_{B}R{T}_{B}} . . . \left(1\right)$

Given ${V}_{A} = {V}_{B}$ and ${T}_{A} = {T}_{B}$.

Thus, from equation (1), it follows that

\begin{cases}\dfrac{PA}{PB}$& = & $\dfrac{nA}{nB}$\\ & = & $\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{32}}$\\ & = & 16\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: The mean free path of molecules of a certain gas at STP is $1500d$, where $d$is the diameter of the gas molecules. While maintaining the standard pressure, the mean free path of the molecules at $373K$ is approximately:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The mean free path is given by the relation,

$\lambda = \dfrac{RT}{\sqrt{2}\pid^{2}{N}_{A}P}$

So,~$\lambda ∝ T$

Let~$\lambda '$~be the new mean free path.

Hence,

$\dfrac{1500d}{\lambda '} = \dfrac{273}{373}$

$⇒ {λ}^{'} = 2049 . 45d \approx 2049d$

questions.q: The correct relation between the degrees of freedom $f$ and the ratio of specific heat $\gamma$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f}$

$f = \dfrac{2}{\gamma - 1}$

questions.q: A gas mixture consists of $8$ moles of argon and $6$ moles of oxygen at temperature $T$. Neglecting all vibrational modes, the total internal energy of the system is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, internal energy is given by, $U = n{C}_{v}T$. Also argon gas is monoatomic and oxygen gas is diatomic.

Therefore, total internal energy will be${U}_{net} = {n}_{1}{C}_{V1}T + {n}_{2}{C}_{V2}T$

$= 8 \times \dfrac{3R}{2} \times T + 6 \times \dfrac{5R}{2} \times T$

$= 27RT$

questions.q: The relation between root mean square speed  \left({v}_{rms}\right)$ and most probable speed  \left({v}_{p}\right)$ for the molar mass $M$ of oxygen gas molecule at the temperature of $300K$ will be&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
RMS speed of& ${O}_{2}$~gas is~${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{32}}$~and most probable speed of~${O}_{2}$~gas is~${v}_{mostprobable} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2RT}{32}}$.

Here temperature is same.

Thus,~$\dfrac{vrms}{vmostprobable} = \dfrac{\dfrac{3RT}{32}}{\dfrac{2RT}{32}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

Hence,~${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}{v}_{p}$

questions.q: When $100 \mathrm{~g}$ of a liquid $\mathrm{A}$ at $100^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ is added to $50 \mathrm{~g}$ of a liquid $B$ at temperature $75^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$, the temperature of the mixture becomes $90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$. The temperature of the mixture, if $100 \mathrm{~g}$ of liquid $A$ at $100^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ is added to $50 \mathrm{~g}$ of liquid $\mathrm{B}$ at $50^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$, will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Heat loss $=$ Heat gain $=\mathrm{mS} \Delta \theta\mathrm{So}, \mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{A}} \Delta \theta_{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{B}} \Delta \theta_{\mathrm{B}}
\Rightarrow 100 \times S_{A} \times(100-90)=50 \times S_{B} \times(90-75)
2 S_{A}=1.5 S_{B} \Rightarrow S_{A}=\frac{3}{4} S_{B}
Now, $100 $\times \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{A}} \times($100-$\theta)=$50 $\times \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{B}} \times(\theta-$50)2 $\times\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) \times($100-$\theta)=(\theta-$50)
300-3 $\theta=$2 $\theta-$100
400=5 $\theta \Rightarrow \theta=$80^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} C

questions.q: The average kinetic energy of a molecule of the gas is
options: dependent on the nature of the gas
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
3}{2}RT$.

Average kinetic energy~of one molecule of gas~$= \dfrac{3}{2}kT ( k = \dfrac{R}{NA} )$

Where~$k$~is~Boltzmann~constant and~$T$& is absolute temperature.

So, from above relation we can say average kinetic energy of molecule is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.q: Consider a gas of triatomic molecules. The molecules& are assumed to be triangular and made of massless rigid rods whose vertices are occupied by atoms. The internal energy of a mole of the gas at temperature T is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula of internal energy of a gas is given by

$U = \dfrac{f}{2}RT$

Here~$R$~is the gas constant and $T$~is temperature.

\left(R = 8 . 314J{mol}^{- 1}K^{- 1}\right)$

For the given configuration of triatomic molecules, the degree of freedom~$f = 6$

$⇒ U = \dfrac{6}{2}RT = 3RT$

$

questions.q: The volume $V$ of an enclosure contains a mixture of three gases, $16g$ of oxygen,~$28g$~of nitrogen and $44g$ of carbon dioxide at absolute temperature $T$. Consider $R$ as universal gas constant. The pressure of the mixture of gases is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$PV = \left({n}_{1} + {n}_{2} + {n}_{3}\right)RT$

$P \times V = \left[\dfrac{16}{32} + \dfrac{28}{28} + \dfrac{44}{44}\right]RT$

$PV = \left[\dfrac{1}{2} + 1 + 1\right]RT$

$P = \dfrac{5}{2}\dfrac{RT}{V}$

questions.q: The root mean square speed of molecules of nitrogen gas at $27 ° C$ is approximately: (Given mass of a nitrogen molecule $= 4 . 6 \times {10}^{- 26}kg$ and take Boltzmann constant ${k}_{B} = 1 . 4 \times {10}^{- 23}JK^{- 1}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The RMS value of a gas is given by&

${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3{k}_{B}T}{m}}$

Substituting the given values,

${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3 \times 1 . 4 \times {10}^{- 23} \times 300}{4 . 6 \times {10}^{- 26}}}$
$\approx 523ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: During an adiabatic process, if the pressure of a gas is found to be proportional to the cube of its absolute temperature, then the ratio of $\frac{C_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}}$ for the gas is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{P} \propto \mathrm{T}^3 \\
& \mathrm{PT}^{-3}=\text { constant } \\
& \because \frac{\mathrm{PV}}{\mathrm{T}}=\mathrm{nR}=\text { constant from ideal gas equation } \\
& (\mathrm{P})(\mathrm{PV})^{-3}=\text { constant } \\
& \mathrmP^{-2} \mathrm{~V}^{-3}=\text { cosntant }...(i)
\end{aligned}\because$ Process equation for adiabatic process is
$\mathrm{PV}^{\mathrm{y}}=\text { constant }...(ii)$
Comparing equation (1) and (2)
$\frac{C_P}{C_V}=y=\frac{3}{2}$

questions.q: What will be the average value of energy for a monoatomic gas in thermal equilibrium at temperature $T ?$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As per Equi-partition law,

each degree of freedom contributes
$\dfrac{1}{2}{k}_{B}T$~average energy.

In mono atomic gas, $D . O . F .= 3$
$⇒$ Average energy~$= 3 \times \dfrac{1}{2}{k}_{B}T = \dfrac{3}{2}{k}_{B}T$

questions.q: The plot that depicts the behavior of the mean free time $τ$ (time between two successive collisions) for the molecules of an ideal gas, as a function of temperature \left(T\right),$ qualitatively, is: (Graphs are schematic and not drawn to scale)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The average time taken& by a moving particle between successive collisions or impacts is referred to as the mean free time \left(τ\right)$.

The average distance a moving particle travels between successive collisions or impacts is referred to as the mean free path \left(\lambda\right)$.

$\lambda = \dfrac{kT}{\sqrt{2}\pid^{2}P}$

and~${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

So, the mean free time~$τ = \dfrac{λ}{vrms}$

Therefore,~$τ ∝ \dfrac{1}{T}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I :The average momentum of a molecule in a sample of an ideal gas depends on temperature.

Statement II : The rms speed of oxygen molecules in a gas is $v$. If the temperature is doubled and the oxygen molecules dissociate into oxygen atoms, the rms speed will become $2v$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Momentum is a vector quantity and average momentum of molecules of a sample is zero due to random motion.

${P}_{avg} = 0$

RMS speed of a molecule is given by

${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

Now the temperature is doubled~${T}_{new} = 2T$~and due to dissociation~${M}_{new} = \dfrac{M}{2}$.

$⇒ \dfrac{vnew}{v} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2T}{\dfrac{M}{2}}}{\dfrac{T}{M}}$

$⇒ {v}_{new} = 2v$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a diatomic molecule, the rotational energy at a given temperature obeys Maxwell's distribution.

Statement II : In a diatomic molecule, the rotational energy at a given temperature equals the translational kinetic energy for each molecule.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement $I$~is false but Statement $II$ is true.
Statement $I$ is true but Statement $II$ is false.
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are true.
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are false.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The translational kinetic energy & rotational kinetic energy both obey Maxwell's distribution
independent of each other.
Translational kinetic energy of diatomic molecules $= \dfrac{3}{2}kT$
Rotational kinetic energy of diatomic molecules $= \dfrac{2}{2}kT$
So statement I is true but statement II is false.

questions.q: Assuming the nitrogen molecule is moving with& $r . m . s$. velocity at~$400K$, the de-Broglie wave length of nitrogen molecule is close to : (Given : nitrogen molecule weight :~$4 .64 \times {10}^{- 26}kg$, Boltzman constant :~$1 .38 \times {10}^{- 23}JK^{- 1}$, Planck constant :~$6 .63 \times {10}^{- 34}Js$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{2mk} = \dfrac{h}{m \times \dfrac{3}{2}kT} = \dfrac{h}{3mkT}$

$= \dfrac{6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34}}{3 \times 4 . 64 \times {10}^{- 26} \times 1 . 38 \times {10}^{- 13} \times 400} = 0 . 24\overset{°}{A}$

questions.q: A metal ball of mass $0.1 \mathrm{~kg}$ is heated upto $500^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ and dropped into a vessel of heat capacity $800 \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$ and containing $0.5 \mathrm{~kg}$ water. The initial temperature of water and vessel is $30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$. What is the approximate percentage increment in the temperature of the water? [Specific Heat Capacities of water and metal are, respectively, $4200 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-}{ }^{1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$ and $400 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Assume final temperature $=\mathrmT^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ Heat lass $=$ Heat gain $=\mathrm{ms} \Delta \mathrm{T}\Rightarrow \mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{s}_{\mathrm{B}} \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{w}} \mathrm{s}_{\mathrm{w}} \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{w}}0.1 \times 400 \times(500-\mathrm{T})\quad=0.5 \times 4200 \times(\mathrm{T}-30)+800(\mathrm{~T}-30)\Rightarrow 40(500-\mathrm{T})=(\mathrm{T}-30)(2100+800)\Rightarrow 20000-40 \mathrm{~T}=2900 \mathrm{~T}-30 \times 2900\Rightarrow 20000+30 \times 2900=\mathrm{T}(2940)\mathrm{T}=30.4^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}\frac{\Delta \mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{T}} \times 100=\frac{6.4}{30} \times 100=21 \%$ so the closest answer is $20 \%$.
